questions.question_text: Which development contributed significantly to the formal establishment of modern nursing education in Ghana?

choices.text: The introduction of formal hospital-based nurse training programmes
The replacement of all hospitals with traditional healing centres
The abolition of practical clinical instruction
The restriction of nursing education to informal apprenticeships

questions.rationale: Formal hospital-based training helped establish structured nursing education in Ghana. It provided supervised clinical experience and organised instruction to prepare nurses for professional practice.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana's Code of Professional Conduct?

choices.text: To determine the salaries of all nurses in Ghana
To provide professional and ethical standards that guide nursing practice
To replace every hospital's clinical policy
To regulate the financial activities of health facilities

questions.rationale: The Code establishes standards of professional behaviour and ethical responsibilities for nurses and midwives. It guides practitioners in protecting patients and maintaining public confidence in the profession.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle recognises a patient's right to make informed decisions about their healthcare?

choices.text: Justice
Beneficence
Autonomy
Non-maleficence

questions.rationale: Autonomy is the ethical principle that respects an individual's right to make voluntary and informed decisions. Nurses support autonomy by providing understandable information and respecting valid patient choices.

questions.question_text: The ethical principle of beneficence requires a nurse to:

choices.text: Act in ways intended to promote the patient's wellbeing
Disclose all patient information to relatives
Avoid treating patients who refuse recommended care
Provide care only to patients who can afford it

questions.rationale: Beneficence means acting for the benefit of the patient and promoting their welfare. It involves providing appropriate care, preventing harm where possible and supporting positive health outcomes.

questions.question_text: Which ethical principle is most directly concerned with avoiding the infliction of unnecessary harm?

choices.text: Justice
Autonomy
Non-maleficence
Beneficence

questions.rationale: Non-maleficence means avoiding actions that cause unnecessary harm or injury. Nurses apply this principle by following safe procedures, checking medications and practising within their competence.

questions.question_text: In nursing practice, negligence is best described as:

choices.text: A disagreement between a nurse and a patient's relative
A failure to exercise the standard of care reasonably expected, resulting in harm
A patient's refusal to follow a treatment plan
Any clinical outcome that is not favourable

questions.rationale: Negligence involves a breach of a duty of care that causes legally recognisable harm. An unfavourable outcome alone does not establish negligence; the relevant duty, breach, causation and damage must be considered.

questions.question_text: What is informed consent in healthcare?

choices.text: Permission obtained after a patient receives relevant information and makes a voluntary decision
Permission assumed whenever a patient enters a hospital
Approval given only by the nurse responsible for the patient
A signature obtained without explaining the proposed procedure

questions.rationale: Informed consent requires adequate information, decision-making capacity, understanding and voluntariness. A signature alone does not necessarily demonstrate valid informed consent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental right recognised in Ghana's Patients' Charter?

choices.text: The right to receive every requested treatment regardless of clinical indication
The right to access personal health information and receive appropriate explanations about care
The right to demand confidential information about another patient
The right to disregard all facility safety procedures

questions.rationale: The Patients' Charter recognises patients' rights to information, participation in care, privacy and confidentiality, among other protections. These rights do not mean that patients can demand clinically inappropriate treatment or violate other patients' rights.

questions.question_text: A nurse's scope of practice is primarily determined by:

choices.text: Personal confidence and willingness to perform a procedure
The instructions of any patient receiving care
Professional registration, recognised competencies, applicable standards and relevant laws
The number of years the nurse has worked in one facility alone

questions.rationale: Scope of practice defines the professional activities a practitioner is authorised and competent to perform. It is guided by registration, professional standards, competence and applicable legal and institutional requirements.

questions.question_text: Which action is an example of maintaining appropriate professional boundaries?

choices.text: Accepting expensive gifts from a patient in exchange for special attention
Developing a romantic relationship with a current patient
Using a patient's personal information for private entertainment
Maintaining a therapeutic relationship focused on the patient's care and welfare

questions.rationale: Professional boundaries preserve the therapeutic nature of the nurse-patient relationship. Nurses must avoid exploiting patients, pursuing inappropriate personal relationships or using their professional position for personal gain.

questions.question_text: What is the primary role of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana?

choices.text: To regulate nursing and midwifery education and professional practice
To negotiate salaries exclusively for nurses in public hospitals
To manage the daily operations of every district hospital
To provide health insurance to all registered nurses

questions.rationale: The Nursing and Midwifery Council is the statutory regulatory body responsible for regulating nursing and midwifery education and practice in Ghana. Its functions include registration, licensing and professional discipline within its legal mandate.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the role of the Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association (GRNMA)?

choices.text: It issues professional licences to all nurses and midwives
It represents and promotes the professional and welfare interests of its members
It investigates and determines every case of professional misconduct as the statutory regulator
It accredits all nursing training institutions on behalf of the government

questions.rationale: GRNMA is a professional association that represents nurses and midwives and promotes their professional and welfare interests. It is distinct from the Nursing and Midwifery Council, which has statutory regulatory responsibilities.

questions.question_text: Which educational approach is particularly important in preparing nurses for evidence-based practice?

choices.text: Relying exclusively on traditional practices without reviewing evidence
Avoiding research findings during clinical decision-making
Integrating research evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences
Using examination scores as the only measure of clinical competence

questions.rationale: Evidence-based practice integrates the best available research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values. This approach supports safe, effective and individualised nursing care.

questions.question_text: In nursing, patient advocacy primarily involves:

choices.text: Supporting and protecting patients' rights, interests and informed choices
Making all healthcare decisions on behalf of competent patients
Preventing patients from asking questions about their treatment
Giving priority to the interests of hospital management over patient safety

questions.rationale: Patient advocacy involves supporting patients to understand their options, exercise their rights and receive appropriate care. It also requires nurses to raise concerns when patients' safety or dignity is threatened.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes an important feature of the development of nursing in Ghana?

choices.text: Nursing developed without any contribution from formal health institutions
Nursing education and practice evolved alongside the expansion of healthcare services and professional regulation
Nursing remained exclusively a volunteer activity after independence
Professional nursing registration was replaced by informal community approval

questions.rationale: The development of nursing in Ghana has involved changes in education, healthcare delivery and professional regulation. These developments helped establish nursing as a recognised profession with defined responsibilities and standards.

questions.question_text: Which term describes the professional obligation of a nurse to answer for their decisions, actions and omissions?

choices.text: Delegation
Advocacy
Accountability
Confidentiality

questions.rationale: Accountability means being answerable for one's professional conduct and the consequences of one's actions or omissions. Nurses must be able to justify their decisions and practise according to professional and legal standards.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best distinguishes professional malpractice from an ordinary clinical error?

choices.text: Malpractice concerns a professional breach of the expected standard of care that causes harm
Malpractice occurs whenever a patient is dissatisfied with a nurse
Malpractice applies only when a nurse intentionally injures a patient
Malpractice is established whenever a patient remains in hospital for several days

questions.rationale: Professional malpractice generally refers to professional negligence involving a failure to meet the applicable standard of care, resulting in harm. A clinical error or poor outcome does not automatically establish malpractice without the relevant legal elements.

questions.question_text: A nurse who performs a procedure without valid consent, when consent is required and no lawful exception applies, may be liable for:

choices.text: Defamation
Battery or another applicable civil wrong
Breach of contract by the patient
Professional promotion

questions.rationale: Performing an unauthorised physical intervention may amount to battery under applicable legal principles. The nurse should obtain valid consent or establish that a recognised legal exception applies before proceeding.

questions.question_text: A nurse distributes limited clinical resources according to patients' needs and fair criteria. Which ethical principle is being applied?

choices.text: Autonomy
Non-maleficence
Justice
Fidelity

questions.rationale: Justice concerns fairness and equitable treatment in healthcare. It requires nurses to avoid discrimination and support the fair allocation of available resources according to appropriate criteria.

questions.question_text: A newly employed nurse is asked to perform a procedure that is outside the nurse's demonstrated competence. What is the most appropriate initial response?

choices.text: Perform the procedure to avoid disappointing the senior nurse
Ask a colleague to document that the procedure was supervised
Explain the limitation, seek appropriate supervision or training, and ensure patient safety
Delegate the procedure to any available person

questions.rationale: Nurses must recognise the limits of their competence and avoid undertaking procedures they cannot perform safely. They should seek appropriate support, supervision or training while ensuring that the patient's care needs are addressed.

questions.question_text: A conscious adult patient with decision-making capacity refuses a recommended blood transfusion after receiving an adequate explanation. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Administer the transfusion because the healthcare team considers it beneficial
Respect the informed refusal, communicate it to the responsible clinician and document the discussion
Ask the patient's relative to override the patient's decision
Discharge the patient immediately without further discussion

questions.rationale: A competent adult generally has the right to refuse treatment, even when the decision may carry significant health risks. The nurse should ensure the patient understands the consequences, notify the responsible clinician and document the refusal and relevant discussions.

questions.question_text: A patient at a district hospital asks the nurse to explain the purpose and possible risks of a proposed procedure. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Tell the patient that only relatives are entitled to receive medical information
Explain the information within the nurse's competence and refer questions requiring further clinical explanation to the responsible clinician
Tell the patient to sign the consent form before asking questions
Avoid answering because patients are not expected to participate in treatment decisions

questions.rationale: Patients have a right to understandable information about their care and to participate in decisions. Nurses should provide accurate information within their competence and ensure that the responsible clinician addresses questions beyond their role.

questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that a patient who speaks only a local Ghanaian language does not understand the explanation of a treatment plan. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Proceed because the treatment has already been prescribed
Ask another patient to interpret the discussion
Arrange a suitable interpreter and confirm the patient's understanding
Obtain a signature from the patient's relative without involving the patient

questions.rationale: Effective communication is necessary for informed decision-making and respect for autonomy. A suitable interpreter should be used where needed, and the nurse should confirm that the patient understands the relevant information.

questions.question_text: A nurse receives a friend request from a current patient on a personal social media account. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Accept the request and discuss the patient's treatment online
Decline the request and maintain professional communication through approved healthcare channels
Accept the request but share only selected clinical details
Ask the patient to post a positive review in exchange for accepting

questions.rationale: Personal social media relationships with current patients can blur professional boundaries and create confidentiality risks. Nurses should maintain appropriate professional communication and follow facility policies on social media use.

questions.question_text: A nurse delegates routine observations to an appropriately trained healthcare assistant. Which responsibility remains with the nurse?

choices.text: Ensuring that the delegated task is appropriate and that the required supervision and follow-up occur
Assuming that delegation removes all professional responsibility
Allowing the assistant to interpret all abnormal findings independently
Permitting the assistant to delegate the task to an untrained visitor

questions.rationale: Delegation does not remove the nurse's responsibility to assess whether the task is appropriate and whether the person has the necessary competence. The nurse must provide suitable instructions, supervision and follow-up in accordance with professional standards and facility policy.

questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a medication administration record contains an incorrect entry made earlier in the shift. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Erase the entry completely so that the record appears correct
Leave the error because another nurse made it
Correct the record according to documentation policy while preserving the original entry and making the correction traceable
Create a second record and destroy the original

questions.rationale: Clinical records must be accurate, complete and traceable. Corrections should follow the facility's approved documentation procedure and must not conceal or falsify the original entry.

questions.question_text: A patient's relative asks a nurse to disclose the patient's HIV status. The patient has not authorised disclosure, and no lawful exception is apparent. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Disclose the status because the person is a close relative
Maintain confidentiality and explain that disclosure requires appropriate authorisation or another lawful basis
Discuss the status in the hospital waiting area
Give the relative access to the patient's entire medical record

questions.rationale: Confidentiality is a fundamental professional and patient right. Information should not be disclosed merely because someone is a relative; disclosure must be authorised or otherwise legally justified.

questions.question_text: A registered nurse in Ghana has a concern about the renewal of a professional practising licence. Which organisation should the nurse contact for regulatory guidance?

choices.text: Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association
National Health Insurance Authority
Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana
District Assembly

questions.rationale: The Nursing and Midwifery Council is responsible for professional registration and licensing within its statutory mandate. GRNMA represents professional and welfare interests but does not replace the Council as the licensing regulator.

questions.question_text: A nurse observes that a colleague repeatedly administers medications without checking patients' identities. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Ignore the practice because the colleague has more experience
Take appropriate immediate steps to protect affected patients and report the unsafe practice through the established channels
Post the colleague's name and conduct on social media
Wait until a patient suffers serious harm before raising the concern

questions.rationale: Patient safety requires prompt action when an unsafe practice is identified. The nurse should address any immediate risk and report the concern through appropriate supervisory or institutional channels, documenting relevant facts objectively.

questions.question_text: A nurse working in a rural health facility enrols in an accredited continuing professional development programme. What is the main professional benefit?

choices.text: It automatically authorises the nurse to perform every advanced clinical procedure
It supports the maintenance and development of knowledge and clinical competence
It removes the need for professional registration
It guarantees promotion regardless of performance

questions.rationale: Continuing professional development helps nurses maintain current knowledge, improve skills and adapt to changes in healthcare. Participation does not automatically expand a nurse's legal scope of practice or guarantee promotion.

questions.question_text: A nurse is explaining the contribution of community-based nursing to healthcare development in Ghana. Which example best demonstrates this contribution?

choices.text: Providing health education, preventive services and basic care within communities
Restricting all nursing activities to specialist teaching hospitals
Replacing all referral hospitals with community volunteers
Limiting nursing practice to administrative duties

questions.rationale: Community-based nursing extends healthcare beyond hospitals through prevention, health education and essential services. It contributes to improving access to care, particularly in underserved communities.

questions.question_text: Two patients require urgent attention, but only one nurse is immediately available. One patient has severe respiratory distress, while the other has a minor wound. Which action best reflects the principle of justice?

choices.text: Attend to the patient who arrived first, regardless of clinical condition
Attend to the patient with severe respiratory distress first and arrange care for the other patient
Attend to the patient who is able to pay immediately
Allow the patients' relatives to decide who receives care first

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair allocation of care according to relevant clinical needs rather than wealth or social status. The patient with severe respiratory distress has the more immediate threat to life and should receive urgent attention.

questions.question_text: A nurse accidentally administers a medication to the wrong patient. The patient is currently asymptomatic. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Wait to see whether symptoms develop before informing anyone
Document that the correct medication was administered
Immediately assess the patient, inform the responsible clinician, follow safety procedures and report the incident accurately
Ask the patient not to mention the incident to anyone

questions.rationale: A medication error requires prompt assessment and action to reduce the risk of harm, even when the patient has no immediate symptoms. The nurse must report and document the event honestly in accordance with institutional policy.

questions.question_text: A patient at a health centre complains that staff members discuss clinical details loudly where other patients can hear. Which patient right is most directly being compromised?

choices.text: The right to privacy and confidentiality
The right to choose a preferred hospital building
The right to receive unlimited medication
The right to avoid all clinical assessments

questions.rationale: Discussing identifiable clinical information where unauthorised people can hear may breach privacy and confidentiality. Nurses should use appropriate private settings when communicating sensitive patient information.

questions.question_text: A patient gives a nurse an expensive gift and asks the nurse to ensure that the patient receives preferential treatment. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Accept the gift because refusing it may offend the patient
Accept the gift but provide preferential care only when possible
Politely decline the gift, explain professional expectations and provide care according to clinical need
Ask the patient to give the gift to another nurse instead

questions.rationale: Accepting expensive gifts linked to preferential treatment can create conflicts of interest and compromise professional boundaries. Care should be provided fairly according to clinical need and professional standards.

questions.question_text: A nurse working at a CHPS compound identifies a patient whose condition requires diagnostic investigations and specialist management unavailable at the facility. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Attempt every procedure independently to avoid referral
Stabilise the patient within the nurse's competence and arrange an appropriate referral
Send the patient home with advice to return if the condition worsens
Ask an untrained community member to manage the condition

questions.rationale: CHPS services provide essential community-based care but do not replace higher-level services when a patient's condition requires them. The nurse should provide appropriate initial care and arrange timely referral through the established referral system.

questions.question_text: A nurse notices that a patient is being denied appropriate care because the patient cannot immediately pay a requested fee. What is the nurse's most appropriate action?

choices.text: Ignore the situation because financial matters are unrelated to nursing
Advocate for assessment of the patient's clinical needs and help clarify available financial or NHIS procedures
Promise that every service will be free under NHIS
Tell the patient to leave and seek care elsewhere

questions.rationale: Nurses should advocate for equitable access to clinically necessary care and help patients understand available support and payment arrangements. NHIS coverage depends on applicable benefits and eligibility, so nurses should not promise that every service is free.

questions.question_text: A group of nurses wants to raise concerns about working conditions and professional welfare through their professional association. Which organisation is most directly relevant?

choices.text: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana
Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association
Food and Drugs Authority
National Health Insurance Authority

questions.rationale: GRNMA represents the interests of nurses and midwives in professional and welfare matters. The Nursing and Midwifery Council has a separate statutory role in regulating professional education and practice.

questions.question_text: A nursing student uses an electronic learning platform to access lectures, participate in discussions and complete assessments. Which trend in nursing education does this illustrate?

choices.text: Abandonment of professional education standards
Technology-supported and blended learning
Replacement of all clinical placements with online activities
Informal learning without assessment

questions.rationale: Electronic learning platforms support technology-enhanced and blended education by combining digital learning activities with other forms of instruction. They complement rather than automatically replace supervised clinical learning.

questions.question_text: A nurse is assigned to a community outreach programme that includes health education, immunisation support and referral of clients with danger signs. Which broader development in Ghanaian nursing does this best demonstrate?

choices.text: The movement of nursing practice towards hospital-only services
The expansion of nursing roles in primary healthcare and community health services
The removal of preventive healthcare from nursing responsibilities
The replacement of professional nurses with unregulated practitioners

questions.rationale: Nursing in Ghana has expanded beyond hospital-based treatment to include prevention, health promotion and community-based services. These functions are important in primary healthcare and initiatives such as CHPS.

questions.question_text: A nurse is preparing to administer a medication but notices that the prescription is unclear. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Estimate the intended dose based on previous experience
Ask another patient what dose is usually given
Clarify the prescription with the authorised prescriber before administration
Administer half of the suspected dose without consultation

questions.rationale: An unclear prescription creates a risk of medication error and patient harm. The nurse should seek clarification from the authorised prescriber and avoid administering medication until the order is sufficiently clear and valid.

questions.question_text: A nurse is caring for a patient whose religious beliefs influence the patient's decision about a proposed treatment. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Dismiss the patient's beliefs because clinical decisions are exclusively professional matters
Explore the patient's concerns respectfully and discuss clinically appropriate options
Force the patient to accept the treatment to prevent disagreement
Stop providing all nursing care to the patient

questions.rationale: Respect for autonomy requires nurses to take patients' values and beliefs seriously while providing accurate clinical information. The nurse should explore acceptable options without coercion and continue appropriate care.

questions.question_text: A patient complains that a nurse has used insulting language during a dressing procedure. What should the nurse in charge do?

choices.text: Dismiss the complaint because the dressing was completed
Listen respectfully, assess the concern, address the patient's immediate needs and follow the facility's complaint procedure
Tell the patient to complain only after discharge
Warn the patient that making a complaint may delay treatment

questions.rationale: Patients have a right to respectful treatment and an appropriate process for raising concerns. The nurse in charge should respond professionally, protect the patient's dignity and ensure that the complaint is managed through established procedures.

questions.question_text: A nurse is asked by a relative to interpret a laboratory result and independently prescribe medication for a patient. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Prescribe medication because the relative has requested it
Explain that diagnosis and prescribing must be undertaken by an appropriately authorised practitioner and refer the request
Select medication based on the patient's symptoms without further assessment
Ask the relative to purchase antibiotics without a prescription

questions.rationale: Nurses must not undertake activities outside their legal authority and professional competence. Requests for diagnosis or prescribing should be directed to an appropriately authorised practitioner, while the nurse continues to provide care within their scope.

questions.question_text: A nurse has reported repeated shortages of essential emergency supplies to the facility supervisor, but no action has been taken and patient safety remains at risk. What should the nurse do next?

choices.text: Remain silent because the issue has already been reported once
Use the appropriate further reporting or escalation channels and maintain factual records of the concerns
Publish confidential patient records online to attract attention
Remove the supplies from another facility without authorisation

questions.rationale: Persistent threats to patient safety should be escalated through appropriate organisational or regulatory channels when initial reporting does not resolve them. Reports should be factual, responsible and consistent with confidentiality and applicable whistleblowing procedures.

questions.question_text: A nurse who previously cared for a patient is invited to manage the patient's private financial affairs in return for payment. What should the nurse consider most carefully?

choices.text: Whether the payment is higher than the nurse's monthly salary
The risk of exploitation, conflict of interest and inappropriate continuation of a professional relationship
Whether the patient can provide a positive testimonial
Whether other nurses are willing to participate

questions.rationale: Managing a former patient's private financial affairs may create conflicts of interest and expose the patient to exploitation. Nurses should maintain appropriate boundaries and seek guidance where a proposed relationship could compromise professional integrity.

questions.question_text: A nurse is concerned that a colleague is practising with an expired professional licence. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore the matter because professional licensing is voluntary
Encourage the colleague to regularise their registration and raise the concern through appropriate supervisory or regulatory channels
Issue a new licence on behalf of the facility
Allow the colleague to practise independently until a patient complains

questions.rationale: Professional licensing is an important regulatory requirement for lawful nursing practice. The concern should be addressed through appropriate management and regulatory channels rather than ignored or resolved through unauthorised action.

questions.question_text: During an emergency, an unconscious patient requires an urgent life-saving intervention. No authorised representative is immediately available, and delay would place the patient's life at serious risk. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.text: Delay all treatment until a relative arrives, regardless of the danger
Proceed with necessary emergency care under the applicable legal and professional emergency principles
Ask an unrelated visitor to sign consent on behalf of the patient
Refuse to provide care because written consent is unavailable

questions.rationale: Where a patient lacks decision-making capacity and urgent treatment is necessary to prevent serious harm, emergency treatment may proceed under applicable legal principles. The intervention should be limited to what is necessary, with appropriate documentation and subsequent communication where possible.

questions.question_text: A nurse is caring for two patients from different ethnic groups and notices that a colleague gives one patient less attention because of the patient's background. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Accept the difference because healthcare workers may choose whom to assist
Ensure both patients receive fair care based on clinical need and address the discriminatory conduct through appropriate channels
Give both patients exactly the same intervention regardless of their clinical conditions
Transfer the disadvantaged patient without investigating the concern

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair and non-discriminatory treatment. Nurses should ensure that care is based on clinical need and raise concerns about conduct that compromises equitable access or patient dignity.

questions.question_text: A nursing tutor uses simulation to teach students how to respond to a patient experiencing cardiac arrest. What is the main educational advantage of this approach?

choices.text: It removes the need for all clinical supervision
It allows students to practise clinical decision-making and technical skills in a controlled learning environment
It guarantees that every student will respond correctly in every real emergency
It replaces the need to study anatomy and physiology

questions.rationale: Simulation provides a controlled environment in which students can practise technical and non-technical skills, receive feedback and learn from errors without exposing patients to unnecessary risk. It complements supervised clinical placement rather than replacing it.

questions.question_text: A nurse fails to report a patient's rapidly deteriorating condition despite recognising clear warning signs. The delay contributes to serious harm. Which legal concept is most relevant?

choices.text: Negligence arising from a possible breach of the duty to provide appropriate care
Defamation arising from a patient's complaint
Trespass arising from the patient's hospital admission
Vicarious consent arising from the nurse's professional registration

questions.rationale: A nurse has a duty to recognise and respond appropriately to significant changes in a patient's condition. Failure to escalate a deterioration may constitute a breach of the standard of care if it causes harm and the relevant legal elements are established.

questions.question_text: A nurse witnesses a senior staff member deliberately altering patient records to conceal a medication error. What is the most appropriate response?

choices.text: Alter another entry to make the records consistent
Preserve relevant factual information and report the suspected falsification through appropriate channels
Delete the original records to protect the facility's reputation
Discuss the incident publicly using identifiable patient information

questions.rationale: Falsifying clinical records is a serious professional and patient-safety concern. The nurse should not participate in concealment and should report the suspected misconduct through appropriate channels while protecting confidential information.

questions.question_text: A patient at a public hospital asks to know the name and professional role of the nurse providing care. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Refuse because patients are not entitled to identify healthcare workers
Provide appropriate identification and explain the nurse's role in the patient's care
Give the patient the names of all staff members in the facility
Tell the patient to contact the Ministry of Health before receiving an answer

questions.rationale: Patients should be able to identify the healthcare professionals involved in their care and understand their roles. Providing appropriate identification supports transparency, trust and accountability.

questions.question_text: A nurse is assigned to supervise a trainee during a clinical procedure. The trainee appears unsure of the required steps. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Allow the trainee to continue independently to build confidence
Assess the trainee's competence, provide guidance and intervene when necessary to protect the patient
Leave the trainee with the patient while attending to administrative work
Ask the patient to supervise the trainee

questions.rationale: Clinical supervision requires the nurse to assess the learner's ability and provide support appropriate to the task and level of competence. Patient safety takes priority over allowing a trainee to perform an unfamiliar procedure independently.

questions.question_text: A nurse is asked to allocate a limited number of available beds to patients who have similar clinical urgency. Which approach is most ethically appropriate?

choices.text: Allocate beds according to patients' wealth
Use transparent, clinically relevant and non-discriminatory allocation criteria
Give beds only to patients known personally by staff
Allow the loudest relative to determine allocation

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair and consistent allocation of scarce healthcare resources. Transparent criteria based on clinical need and other relevant considerations reduce discrimination and arbitrary decision-making.

questions.question_text: A nurse is instructed to carry out an intervention that appears to be outside the nurse's authorised scope of practice. The supervisor insists that it must be done immediately. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Carry out the intervention because a supervisor's instruction overrides professional standards
Refuse all further duties in the facility
Explain the professional concern, avoid undertaking an unauthorised intervention and seek an appropriate alternative to protect the patient
Ask a patient to perform the intervention instead

questions.rationale: A supervisor's instruction does not automatically authorise a nurse to practise outside legal or professional limits. The nurse must communicate the concern, seek an appropriately authorised practitioner and ensure that the patient's immediate needs are addressed safely.

questions.question_text: A patient develops a serious complication after surgery. The family alleges negligence because the outcome was poor. Which information would be most important in assessing whether negligence occurred?

choices.text: Whether the family was satisfied with the hospital's accommodation
Whether a duty of care existed, the expected standard was breached, the breach caused harm and legally recognised damage occurred
Whether the nurse has worked in the hospital for more than five years
Whether the patient had previously been admitted to the same hospital

questions.rationale: A poor clinical outcome does not by itself prove negligence. The assessment must consider duty of care, breach of the applicable standard, causation and damage, based on the available evidence.

questions.question_text: A competent adult patient refuses a recommended treatment because of personal beliefs. The nurse believes the treatment would substantially improve the patient's health. Which response best balances autonomy and beneficence?

choices.text: Force the patient to accept treatment because beneficence always overrides autonomy
Respect the patient's decision without providing any further information
Explain the benefits, risks and alternatives, explore the patient's concerns and respect the informed decision
Ask the patient's employer to make the decision

questions.rationale: Beneficence supports recommending treatment that may benefit the patient, while autonomy requires respect for a competent patient's informed choice. The nurse should provide balanced information, explore concerns and avoid coercion.

questions.question_text: A nurse shares a photograph of a patient receiving treatment in a ward WhatsApp group without the patient's permission. The nurse argues that the group is made up of healthcare workers. Which professional concern is most significant?

choices.text: The photograph may reduce the hospital's advertising opportunities
The disclosure may breach patient confidentiality and privacy, even within a professional group
The nurse has failed to obtain permission from the hospital cleaner
The patient may demand a different hospital bed

questions.rationale: Patient information and images must be handled confidentially and shared only when there is an appropriate professional and lawful basis. Membership of a healthcare workers' group does not automatically authorise disclosure of identifiable patient information.

questions.question_text: A nurse begins providing private paid care to a current patient outside the facility, without informing the employer or following applicable professional and institutional requirements. The patient becomes dependent on the nurse for personal and financial decisions. What is the most appropriate professional assessment?

choices.text: The arrangement is acceptable because the patient has voluntarily agreed to pay
The arrangement creates potential boundary violations, conflicts of interest and risks of patient exploitation
The arrangement is acceptable as long as the nurse works additional hours
The arrangement is a normal extension of every nurse-patient relationship

questions.rationale: A private financial arrangement with a current patient can create dependency, conflicts of interest and opportunities for exploitation. The nurse should maintain professional boundaries and follow applicable professional and institutional requirements.

questions.question_text: A nurse reports unsafe staffing levels through the facility's internal reporting system. Management threatens disciplinary action unless the nurse withdraws the report, although the safety concern remains unresolved. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: Withdraw the report to avoid conflict with management
Post confidential patient details online to pressure management
Maintain a factual record and seek advice or escalate the concern through appropriate further reporting and whistleblowing channels
Stop documenting all patient care until management responds

questions.rationale: Whistleblowing involves reporting suspected wrongdoing or serious risks through appropriate channels, particularly when internal action has failed. The nurse should preserve relevant evidence, protect patient confidentiality and use applicable organisational and legal reporting mechanisms.

questions.question_text: A nurse argues that GRNMA should issue a practising licence because it represents nurses, while the Nursing and Midwifery Council should negotiate the nurse's salary. Which correction is most accurate?

choices.text: Both organisations have identical statutory responsibilities
GRNMA primarily represents professional and welfare interests, while the Nursing and Midwifery Council regulates nursing and midwifery practice
The Council is responsible only for hospital construction, while GRNMA accredits training institutions
Neither organisation has any formal role in nursing in Ghana

questions.rationale: GRNMA and the Nursing and Midwifery Council have distinct roles in Ghana's nursing sector. GRNMA represents its members' professional and welfare interests, whereas the Council performs statutory regulatory functions, including registration and licensing.

questions.question_text: A nursing school introduces online lectures and simulation laboratories but reduces supervised clinical placements substantially. Students perform well in written examinations but struggle with actual patient care. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.text: Written examinations are sufficient to establish clinical competence
Technology-based teaching should replace all direct patient contact
The programme needs to strengthen supervised clinical learning and ensure that educational methods develop practical competence as well as theoretical knowledge
Students should be allowed to practise independently until their confidence improves

questions.rationale: Nursing education must develop knowledge, practical skills, professional attitudes and clinical judgement. Online learning and simulation are valuable, but they cannot entirely replace appropriately supervised experience in real clinical settings.

questions.question_text: A health administrator proposes that community nursing services should be discontinued because specialist hospitals provide more advanced treatment. Which response best reflects the historical and contemporary development of nursing in Ghana?

choices.text: Community nursing is unnecessary once specialist hospitals are available
Community nursing complements hospital services through prevention, early identification, health education, continuity of care and referral
Community nurses should replace all specialist practitioners
Community nursing is limited to collecting hospital fees

questions.rationale: The development of nursing in Ghana includes an expanding role in primary healthcare and community-based services. Community nursing complements hospital care by improving access, prevention, early intervention and referral rather than replacing specialist services.

questions.question_text: During a disease outbreak, a facility has one available isolation bed. A patient with a highly transmissible infection and significant clinical risk requires isolation, while another patient requests the bed for privacy. Which decision is most ethically defensible?

choices.text: Allocate the bed to the patient who complains most loudly
Allocate the bed according to clinical urgency, infection prevention requirements and transparent facility criteria
Allocate the bed to the patient who offers a financial incentive
Allow both patients to share the bed to avoid making a decision

questions.rationale: Justice requires fair resource allocation using relevant and consistently applied criteria. Infection prevention needs and clinical urgency are legitimate considerations when determining the appropriate use of a scarce isolation bed.

questions.question_text: A nurse gives a prescribed medication without checking the patient's identity. The medication is intended for another patient, and the recipient develops an adverse reaction. Which statement best explains the nurse's potential professional and legal exposure?

choices.text: The nurse cannot be responsible because the medication was prescribed by a clinician
The nurse may have breached the expected standard of medication administration, and liability depends on the evidence of causation and harm
Only the patient is responsible for confirming the medication
The nurse is automatically criminally liable whenever an adverse reaction occurs

questions.rationale: Nurses have an independent responsibility to follow medication safety procedures, including checking patient identity. A failure to do so may constitute a breach of the standard of care, although the specific legal consequences depend on the facts and applicable law.

questions.question_text: A nurse discovers that a facility is routinely recording services as provided under NHIS when the services were not actually delivered. The practice may expose patients and the facility to harm. Which action is most appropriate?

choices.text: Participate in the recording because the facility needs additional income
Destroy the records before anyone investigates
Preserve relevant factual information and report the suspected fraud through appropriate institutional and authorised reporting channels
Share identifiable patient records publicly to prove the allegation

questions.rationale: Recording services that were not delivered may constitute fraud and undermine the integrity of healthcare financing. The nurse should not participate in falsification and should report the concern responsibly while protecting confidential patient information.
